caption:
On Sept. 23, at #UNGA81, UNDP will bring more than 58,000 young voices into the conversation at “Sparking the Next Generation of Energy Talent.”

Working with Goodwall, we heard directly from young people around the world on how they see their roles in the energy transition. And their engagement was encouraging:
- "Give us the skills, give us the affordable tools, and we will be powering Kenya's digital future."
- "Every hour of darkness is an hour of lost potential... In Nigeria, we have some of the most abundant sunshine on earth. We just need the will to use it."
By 2030, 1.2 billion young people are expected to enter the global workforce. Fewer than 40% are projected to have the skills needed for the green economy.

Demand for green talent is already accelerating:
☀️ Solar PV supported 7.2 million jobs globally in 2024.
💼 Workers with green skills are hired at a rate 46.6% above the workforce average.
🎓 Only 1 in 20 Gen Z workers has the green skills needed to access these opportunities.

We have listened to more than 58,000 young people about their ambitions, the opportunities they want to pursue and the barriers they face. We are bringing their voices to #UNGA81.

Creating green jobs must be matched by access to relevant skills, work experience, mentorship, networks and finance.

We need stronger links between learning and employment, skills and jobs, ideas and capital, and young talent and the industries emerging through the energy transition.
Young people are the workforce needed to deliver the transition now.

#YouthInEnergy #EnergyForDevelopment #SDG7
